strings.name: Julie Mehretu
strings.summary: Mehretu layers architectural drawings, maps, news images and abstract marks to examine how cities, migration and political history inhabit space. Born in Ethiopia and raised in the United States, she developed a transnational visual language through large paintings and prints. Beyond museum exhibitions, she supports residencies, cultural preservation and young people's access to art.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Combines maps, architecture and political history in large abstract paintings, bringing diaspora and urban space into international contemporary art.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia; moved with her family to Michigan in 1977.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: BA from Kalamazoo College; studied in Dakar; MFA from RISD in 1997.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Historical layers in abstraction
strings.highlights.h1.text: Maps, buildings and news images underlie surfaces reorganized through marks and movement.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Art and public connections
strings.highlights.h2.text: Co-founded the Denniston Hill residency and helped preserve Nina Simone's childhood home.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Delivered RISD's commencement address
strings.timeline.t1.text: Returned to her alma mater for the keynote and an honorary degree, discussing art's imaginative possibilities.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Ensemble shown in Venice
strings.timeline.t2.text: Palazzo Grassi presented paintings from different periods in dialogue with other artists' work.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Major career survey opened
strings.timeline.t3.text: LACMA exhibited paintings and works on paper; the show later traveled to the Whitney and other institutions.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Created the HOWL diptych
strings.timeline.t4.text: Made monumental works for SFMOMA, bringing landscape together with abstract marks.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Mogamma at documenta
strings.timeline.t5.text: Four large canvases at documenta 13 connected urban architecture, collective action and history.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Grey Area at the Guggenheim
strings.timeline.t6.text: A painting series extended her study of architectural remains and historical space.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Received a MacArthur fellowship
strings.timeline.t7.text: Her abstract painting practice gained interdisciplinary recognition and support.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed her MFA training
strings.timeline.t8.text: Finished painting and printmaking at RISD before entering Houston's CORE residency.
